name: Alapin 2...d5: Be2, Na3 setup and the d4/Nb5 trick
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: White breaks the pin with Be2, sends the a3 knight toward b5 and only then strikes with d4. After ...cxd4 the knight hop to b5 hits c7 so the queen must drop back before White recaptures, leaving a three-against-two queenside majority.

name: Alapin 2...d5 trap: early ...Bg4 met by Qb3
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: When Black pins the f3 knight before finishing development, Qb3 hits b7 and f7 at the same time. Taking on f3 lets Bxf7+ drag the king into the open.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6 main line: e5, d4, Nf3, Bc4 and Na3
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: Kick the knight with e5, then develop with Nf3 and Bc4 instead of recapturing on d4. When Black breaks with ...d5, take en passant, castle and bring the a3 knight toward b5.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6: ...dxc3 answered by Ng5 and Qh5
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: If Black grabs on c3, Ng5 teams up with the b3 bishop against f7. A queen trade fails to Bxf7+ and Rxd1 with check, so Black must block with ...e6 and Qh5 adds a third attacker on f7.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6 deep line: ...dxc3 Qe2
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: When Black takes on c3 and threatens to trade queens on the open d-file, the queen steps to e2 to keep queens on and play for Nb5 and kingside pressure.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6 vs ...e6: Bxd5 leaves tripled d-pawns
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: Against the lower-level ...e6, giving the bishop for the d5 knight saddles Black with three d-pawns. Recapture on d4 and aim Nc3 and Bf4 at the weak d5 pawn.

name: Alapin 2...Nf6 vs ...d6/...e6: recapture, Qe2 and Rd1
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: If the knight stays on d5, take back on d4, castle and put the queen on e2 so a rook can come to d1. The queenside follows with Bd2 and Nc3, and a trade on e5 only activates White's rook.

name: Alapin 2...Nc6 trap: the e5 knight gets trapped
videoTitle: CRUSH the Sicilian Defense: The ALAPIN
idea: After the c-pawns trade, a slow ...g6 lets d5 chase the knight. If it jumps to e5, f4 leaves it with no safe square.

name: Grand Prix: Bc4 setup with Qe1 and the kingside attack
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: Develop the king's knight behind the f-pawn, aim the bishop at f7 from c4, castle and play d3. The queen swings e1 to h4 while f5 and Bh6 tear at Black's castled king.

name: Grand Prix: Bb5 version, give the bishop after ...Nd4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: The more professional Bb5 targets the c6 knight. If it jumps to d4, White simply castles and lets the bishop go, then runs the same Qe1-h4, f5 and Bh6 attack.

name: Grand Prix vs ...e6/...d5: keep calm, Bb5+ if Black pushes d4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: Do not capture on d5. If Black closes the centre with ...d4, bring the light-squared bishop out with check before the c3 knight reroutes through e2, then attack the king behind the locked centre.

name: Grand Prix vs ...Nge7: the exception, exd5 and Qe2
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: Here White does take on d5: with the e-file open, Qe2 pins the e7 knight, and Qe5 ideas hit g7 because the c6 knight is pinned by the b5 bishop.

name: Grand Prix trap: loose ...Bg4 punished by Bxf7+ and Ng5+
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: A bishop on g4 with no defender is a target. Bxf7+ pulls the king forward and Ng5+ opens the d1-g4 diagonal, so the queen picks up the bishop.

name: Grand Prix vs 2...e5: King's Gambit-style f4
videoTitle: How to WIN with the Grand Prix Attack!
idea: If Black answers Nc3 with ...e5, f4 still works as a King's Gambit in which Black has spent a tempo on ...c5; a quieter Bc4, d3 and f4 also reaches a good Vienna-like setup.

name: French Wing Gambit: b4, a3 and the d4/e5 wedge
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: Through Nf3 and e5, b4 deflects the c5 pawn and a3 offers a second one. White keeps a broad d4/e5 wedge, develops with Bd3, castles and can push h4-h5 on the kingside.

name: French Wing Gambit: ...Nc6 before ...c5, just d4
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: If Black develops the knight in front of the c-pawn, White plays d4, c3 and Bd3, taking the whole centre with a structurally pleasant French Advance.

name: French Wing Gambit: second pawn declined with ...Nc6
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: When Black ignores a3 and develops, White simply recaptures on b4, then plays c3 and d4 for the same big centre without being a pawn down.

name: French Wing Gambit: ...c4 push, clamp with c3 and b5
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: If Black pushes past with ...c4, c3 supports b4 and ...a5 is met by b5, locking the queenside. With no play there for Black, White grabs kingside space with d4, h4 and g4.

name: French Wing Gambit: ...b6 declining, c3 and d4
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: Against ...b6 White keeps building with c3 and d4. With the b-pawn advanced, the a4-e8 diagonal opens, so Qa4+ tricks against an undefended c6 knight appear.

name: Deferred Wing Gambit vs ...d6: b4 and the full centre
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: After Nf3 and ...d6, b4 gives a wing pawn for a full centre. White plays Bd3, castles, routes the knight a3-c2-e3 and then turns to the kingside, recovering the pawn when convenient.

name: Anti-Accelerated Dragon: Qxd4 and Bb5
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: Against ...g6 the wing gambit makes no sense, so White recaptures with the queen and Bb5 stops ...Nc6 from gaining a tempo on it; taking on c6 if the knight appears leaves Black's pawns damaged.

name: Anti-Accelerated Dragon: ...a6 met by e5
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: If Black kicks the bishop, White can ignore it and push e5 at the f6 knight. The resulting position is chaotic and hard to handle over the board.

name: Deferred Wing vs ...Nc6 and ...d5: c4 and the Rb1 trick
videoTitle: CRUSH French and Sicilian Defense with The Wing Gambit
idea: c4 reopens the position, the en passant recapture gains time, and Rb1 offers the c3 knight. After ...Qxc3+ Bd2 the queen's only safe square is a3, and d5 chases the c6 knight with a crushing queenside attack.

name: Wing Gambit: b4 and a3 at once
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Give the b-pawn immediately to remove Black's c-pawn, offer the a-pawn too, then take the centre and develop as aggressively as possible.

name: a3 Sicilian (Delayed Wing) vs ...Nc6 and ...d5: Na3
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: a3 first keeps the pawn trade on White's terms. After the trades, the a-file is open, so Na3 heads for b5 and c7, and ...a6 does not stop it because that pawn is pinned to the a8 rook.

name: a3 Sicilian trap: d5 and Nc7+ wins the queen back
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: With the queen back on d8, d5 hits the c6 knight. Capturing on d5 allows a queen trade on d5 followed by Nc7+, forking king and queen.

name: a3 Sicilian: ...e5 met by Nb5
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: If Black stakes the centre with ...e5, the knight lands on b5 at once, eyeing c7 and the dark squares Black just weakened.

name: a3 Sicilian vs ...e6: b4 anyway
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: Against ...e6 White still plays b4 when a pawn is on offer; if Black grabs, c3 and d4 build a big centre, followed by Bd3 and f4.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Swap the d-pawn for the c-pawn and offer a second pawn on c3 for fast development and open lines. Black's ...e6 can blunt the c4 bishop, so the attack is less direct than in the Danish.

name: Smith-Morra: giving a third pawn, Danish style
videoTitle: GothamChess 1. e4 ONLY Rating Climb | Part 3 (1200+)
idea: Like the Danish, White can leave c3 and let Black take on b2 as well, getting two long-range bishops aimed at f7 and g7 plus Ng5 ideas.

name: Closed Sicilian: Bb5 system, d4 after ...Nd4
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Bb5 aims to damage the c6 knight's structure; if Black hops to d4 and takes the bishop, White retreats the knight, plays d4 and castles long with a big lead in development.

name: Closed Sicilian vs ...g6: g3 and Bg2 build-up
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: Against Dragon setups, White plays slowly with g3, Bg2, f4 and h3 (to stop ...Ng4), then expands on the kingside with g4 and f5.

name: b3 Sicilian
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: A quiet sideline: the bishop goes to b2 to rake the long diagonal, sometimes traded or redeployed to c4, sidestepping Sicilian theory.

name: French: early Bd3 system
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: An offbeat anti-French where the bishop defends e4 straight away. It looks odd but is full of tricks for players who rely on memorised main lines.

name: French: b3 and Bb2 gambit (Papa-Ticulat/Horwitz)
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: White lets the e4 pawn go so the bishop owns the long diagonal, then follows with Qe2 and queenside castling for a quick attack.

name: French: Orthoschnapp Gambit (shown, not recommended)
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: The queen hits b7 and players new to it struggle to guard f7 against fast development, but Levy flags it as objectively unsound.

name: Two Knights French: e5, d4 and dxc5
videoTitle: GothamChess 1. e4 ONLY Rating Climb | Part 4 (1400+)
idea: Develop both knights first, push e5 when the f6 knight appears, then give up the centre with dxc5 and set up the bishops aiming at h7.

name: Two Knights French trap: Greek gift on h7
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: With the bishop on d3 and the knight ready for g5, castling too early allows Bxh7+, Ng5+ and Qh5 against the bare king.

name: Advance Caro-Kann: Tal's h4 against ...Bf5
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: h4 grabs kingside space and threatens g4 against the f5 bishop; it scores well above the other fourth moves.

name: Advance Caro h4 trap: ...e6 and the bishop is trapped
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: A routine ...e6 lets g4 and f3 or h5 hunt the bishop down; with the h7 pawn behind it, it runs out of squares.

name: Advance Caro h4 h5: Bd3 trade and Nf3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Trade off Black's good bishop, then develop Nf3 and use the g5 square that ...h5 weakened for a bishop, castle and expand with Nd2 and c4.

name: Advance Caro h4 h5 Bd3: ...Qa5+ queen trade offer met by e6
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: When Black offers the queen trade, e6 first breaks up Black's pawns; even with doubled d-pawns White gets a strange endgame where e5 and g5 are lasting weaknesses.

name: Advance Caro h4 h5 Bg5 Qb6 Bd3 (main)
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Bg5 stops ...e6 for a moment; after ...Qb6 the b2 pawn is defended tactically by Bd3, and once Black plays ...e6 White returns to Nd2, Nf3 and c4.

name: Advance Caro Bg5 line: ...Qxb2 met by e6, rook sacrifice
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: If Black grabs b2 before playing ...e6, White pushes e6 anyway and gives up the a1 rook; the queen in the corner gets cut off while Qb3 and Nf3 aim at f7 and Black's undeveloped king.

name: Advance Caro Bg5 line: ...Qxd4 met by Nf3
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: If Black takes on d4 instead of trading bishops, Nf3 gains time on the queen and White aims to win the f5 bishop and push e6.

name: Advance Caro h4 h6: g4 and the e6 pawn sacrifice
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Against ...h6, g4 grabs space; when the bishop retreats, e6 gives a pawn to leave Black with doubled e-pawns and weak light squares once the bishops come off.

name: Advance Caro h4 h6 g4 ...Bd7: h5 locks the kingside
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: If the bishop drops to d7, h5 fixes the kingside pawns; White watches the ...c5 break and prepares f4 and g5, castling only where it is safe.

name: Advance Caro h4 ...Qb6: Nc3 and g4
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: Against the trendy ...Qb6 that skips ...h5, White develops Nc3 and follows with g4, adding a4-a5 to harass the queen.

name: Advance Caro ...c5: dxc5 Nc6 Bb5
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: After dxc5 Nc6, Bb5 provokes ...e6 so Black's light-squared bishop stays locked in, while Be3 helps hold the extra c5 pawn.

name: Advance Caro ...c5: dxc5 Nc6 f4
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: A modern engine idea: f4 props up e5 so White can stubbornly keep the c5 pawn, often followed by c3, b4 and a bishop on d4.

name: Advance Caro ...c5 e6: a3 Bxc5 Qg4
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: In the modern main line, Qg4 hits g7 straight away; a simpler path is Nf3, Bd3, b4 and Bb2.

name: Advance Caro ...c5 e6: a3 Bxc5 Nf3 (simple setup)
videoTitle: CRUSH The Caro-Kann with WGM Nemo Zhou
idea: The normal-person version: Nf3, Bd3, b4 and Bb2 give White an easy game, with Bxh7+ and Ng5 tricks if Black castles carelessly.

name: Fantasy ...Bg4: Bc4, c3 and Qb3 fork
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: After ...Bg4 the c4 bishop eyes f7, and c3 prepares Qb3 hitting f7 and b7 together; if Black just keeps developing, White wins material.

name: Fantasy ...exd4 gambit: Ng5, sacrifice on f7 and e5
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: White leaves d4 alone for quick development; if Black castles into Ng5, sacrificing on f7 and pushing e5 hits the f6 knight, which is pinned to the king on the open f-file.

name: Fantasy 4...Nf6: e5 and c4 chase the knight
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: If Black develops instead of striking with ...e5, kick the knight with e5 and c4, then develop Nc3, both bishops and castle behind a huge centre.

name: Fantasy vs ...g6: Nc3, Bg7, Be3 setup
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: Against a Modern-style ...g6, Be3, Qd2 and queenside castling prepare a g4-h4-h5 pawn storm if Black castles short.

name: Fantasy vs ...g6: e5 clamp
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: Top GMs prefer to lock the centre with e5 and follow up with f4, shutting the g7 bishop out of the game.

name: Fantasy vs ...e6: Be3, Qd2, long castle
videoTitle: 1 Pawn Crushes The Caro-Kann...
idea: Against the solid ...e6, White does not need e5: Be3 or Bf4, Qd2 and queenside castling keep a firm centre and point the pawns at Black's king.

name: Alien Gambit: Ng5 and the knight sacrifice on f7
videoTitle: Crush EVERYONE with the Alien Gambit!
idea: Instead of trading on f6, the knight goes to g5 and gives itself up on f7 when kicked. With the king displaced, White develops Bd3, castles, puts a rook on e1 and lands a knight on e5.

name: Alien Gambit trap: ...Bg4 runs into Ne5+
videoTitle: Crush EVERYONE with the Alien Gambit!
idea: The natural ...Bg4 allows Ne5+, forking king and bishop, so White wins the piece back and keeps a dangerous attack.

name: Alien Gambit vs ...c5: c3, and Bg6+ wins the queen
videoTitle: Crush EVERYONE with the Alien Gambit!
idea: Against the best try ...c5, c3 holds the centre; if Black keeps capturing, Bg6+ deflects the king and the queen takes Black's queen down the open d-file.

name: Alien Gambit vs the cocoon: Bd3, O-O and Re1
videoTitle: Crush EVERYONE with the Alien Gambit!
idea: Against a solid ...Nbd7/...e6 shell the bishop belongs on d3, the rook on e1 and the knight on e5, preparing Qh5+ and Bxh6 to strip the king.

name: Caro-Kann Qe2 system: ...d4 met by Nd1
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: The queen on e2 holds e4; if Black closes the centre with ...d4, the knight drops to d1 heading for f2, and White plays g3, Bg2, d3 and f4 for kingside space.

name: Caro-Kann Qe2 trap: ...Nd7 and Nd6 smothered mate
videoTitle: 10 Chess Traps to Win FAST!!
idea: With the queen on e2 the e7 pawn is pinned, so if Black plays ...Nd7 to avoid doubled pawns, Nd6 is a smothered checkmate.

name: Two Knights Caro trap: Qe2 and Nd6# after ...Nf6/...Nbd7
videoTitle: 10 Chess Traps to Win FAST!!
idea: When Black challenges the e4 knight, Qe2 sets the pin on e7; a careless ...Nbd7 lets the knight land on d6 with mate.

name: Two Knights Caro trap: Qe2 and Nd6# after ...Bf5/...Nd7
videoTitle: 10 Chess Traps to Win FAST!!
idea: The same smothered mate works against the bishop development: after ...Bf5 Qe2, the natural ...Nd7 walks into Nd6#.

name: Hillbilly Attack: Bc4, Bb3 and Qh5
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: White lets e4 go and Qh5 hits f7 with the bishop's help; the aim is to force ...e6 or ...g6, then win the e4 pawn back with a lead in development.

name: Caro-Kann: Nc3 and f3 gambit (Blackmar-Diemer style)
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: After ...dxe4, f3 turns the Caro into a Blackmar-Diemer-style gambit for quick development and the f-file, although the pawn on c6 makes it a bit less potent.

name: Exchange Caro-Kann: Bd3, c3, Bf4 and Qb3
videoTitle: GothamChess 1. e4 ONLY Rating Climb | Part 1 (800+)
idea: A simple beginner system: Bd3 and c3 keep the knight off b4, Bf4 develops, and once the c8 bishop leaves, Qb3 attacks the weak b7 pawn.

name: Pirc: h3 and g4 system
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: h3 rules out ...Bg4 and ...Ng4, then g4 and Bg2 start a pawn storm; White can also add Be3 and Qd2 to trade the g7 bishop and castle long.

name: Modern without ...Nf6: Nf3, Bc4, Qe2 and e5
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: When Black delays ...Nf6, White develops Nf3 and Bc4 and prepares an early Qe2 and e5 push, castling and putting a rook on d1.

name: Monkey's Bum: Bc4, Qf3 and the d4 pawn offer
videoTitle: THE MONKEY'S BUM | TRICKY CHESS GAMBIT
idea: Bc4 and Qf3 aim at f7 and force ...e6; then d4 offers a pawn so Ne2 gains time on the bishop, and White castles long and pushes h4-h5.

name: Monkey's Bum trap: ...Nf6 runs into e5
videoTitle: THE MONKEY'S BUM | TRICKY CHESS GAMBIT
idea: With Qf3 and Bc4 eyeing f7, developing the g8 knight is a mistake: e5 attacks it and it cannot move without allowing Qxf7 mate.

name: Scandinavian: Nf3, Be2, castle and the b4 storm vs long castling
videoTitle: Learn to CRUSH with 1. e4 | 10-Minute Chess Openings
idea: White keeps the d-pawn back so Black has no target, castles quickly, and if Black castles long, h3, Nc3 and b4 start a fast queenside pawn storm.

name: Lionheart Gambit vs ...Qa5: b4, Nb5 and Bc4
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: b4 deflects the queen so c7 loses its guard and the b-file opens; Nb5 hits c7 and Bc4 adds pressure on f7.

name: Lionheart trap: Bxf7+, Qh5+ and a discovered attack
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: If Black kicks the b5 knight, Bxf7+ and Qh5+ line both queens up on the fifth rank; the knight then moves with check and uncovers an attack on Black's queen.

name: Lionheart: ...Na6 defending c7, Nf3
videoTitle: TOP 8 BEST Chess Openings
idea: If Black covers c7 with ...Na6, White just develops Nf3, and a knight left on a6 can later be taken to damage Black's pawns.

name: Tennison Gambit: ICBM trap
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: If Black chases the g5 knight with ...h6, Nxf7 and Bg6+ clear the d-file so the queen flies to d8 and wins Black's queen.

name: Tennison: ...e6, then Qf3, Nc3, Bf4 and long castle
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: A pawn down, White develops fast with Qf3, Nc3, Bf4 and queenside castling, then storms with h4 and g4.

name: Tennison: Bc4 and Nc3 win back e4
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: Rather than gambiting more, Bc4 forces ...e6 and Nc3 piles on e4; Qe2 defends if needed and White regains the pawn before playing d4.

name: Tennison vs ...Bf5: g4 wild option
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: The wild try chases the bishop with g4 and develops Bg2 against e4, usually followed by Nc3; h4 ideas exist but ...h5 answers them.

name: Tennison vs ...Bf5: Nc3, d3 and Qf3
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: After ...Nf6, d3 opens lines and Qf3 hits the f5 bishop and the b7 pawn together, buying fast development for the pawn.

name: Nf3 vs ...d5 ...d4: c3
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: If Black pushes past with ...d4, White is already developing freely and c3 immediately challenges the advanced pawn.

name: Scandinavian into the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit
videoTitle: EVERY Chess Gambit for White and Black | Chess Opening Tips
idea: Instead of taking on d5, White offers the e-pawn and then the f-pawn to open the f-file, develop everything at speed and castle long behind the d-file.

name: Tennison vs ...Bf5 Qf3: ...Qc8 met by trades on d3
videoTitle: INTERCONTINENTAL BALLISTIC MISSILE GAMBIT
idea: When Black guards both targets with ...Qc8, White trades on d3 and recaptures with the queen, a pawn down but ahead in development with Bf4, long castling and h4 to come.

name: Alien Gambit vs ...Bf5: Ne5+ at once
videoTitle: Crush EVERYONE with the Alien Gambit!
idea: If Black develops the bishop to f5, the knight jumps to e5 with check straight away, and g4 can follow to drive the bishop off the e6/f7 squares it guards.
